sc30_distinction: SC30 asked whether the fetal cardiomyocyte label is fetal-only and STOPped because the label appears in 81 adult cells (n_query_only=0). SC33 does not reopen that STOP. SC33 asks a different question: whether a within-atlas leave-one-cell-type-out probe trained on the heart atlas itself flags a held-out heart cell type as novel. Fetal cardiomyocyte remains a heart label; if it is underpowered in the held adult donor it is excluded, not re-tested as a fetal-only discovery.
preregistration_note: Heart type lists with n_total>=60 are frozen here for the adult primary sweep and the fetal secondary sweep before any novelty AUROC is computed. Donor splits are locked. Types with n_in_held_donor<30 on the FULL stratum are listed as underpowered and excluded; no alternate donor fold is fabricated.
primary_stratum_justification: The atlas mixes adult (D2–D7, n=29779) and fetal (BRC*+alexsc, n=30889) donors. Mixing developmental stages would reintroduce a confound of the same class as the SC31 cross-atlas protocol shift: novelty could detect adult-vs-fetal rather than a held-out cell type. Adult-only is therefore the primary replication face. Held test donor is D2 (largest adult donor whose 10x 3' v3 fraction is typical of adult, ~10%) and calibration is D3. D6 is kept in train because it is the only adult donor with substantial 10x 3' v3 (~44%); holding D6 out would make chemistry a competing novelty signal.
fetal_secondary_justification: Fetal-only is powered (7 donors, 16 types with n>=60 if held=BRC2260). It is reported as a secondary, not used for protocol_replicates, because the replication target is the SC31 within-atlas adult-lung face and because fetal chemistry is almost entirely 10x 3' v3.
metric_preregistered: per-type AUROC of (1-max softmax) on held-donor remaining types vs held-donor cells of the removed type; bootstrap 95% CI n_boot=200; label-shuffle null; acc@80cov vs forced on the mixed held-donor test set
split: donor-held-out donor_id; temperature on cal donor only; never random cells; adult primary and fetal secondary are separate sweeps
features: HVG(1000)+PCA(30)+logistic; fit on remaining types in train donors only; identical to SC31

subsample.method: stratified by donor with largest-remainder quotas; per LOTO fold, union with ALL cells of the held-out type so n_held equals the full-stratum held-donor count

protocol_replicates_rule: PRIMARY adult median AUROC within 0.1 of 0.777 AND detected ratio >= 0.7
sibling_mechanism: SC31 failure mode: NK cell AUROC 0.333 with nearest remaining centroid T cell. Pre-registered here: a failure matches that pattern if the nearest remaining centroid is in the same sibling group and/or its Euclidean distance is at or below the median nearest-centroid distance of scored types. If failures lack a close sibling, the mechanism claim weakens.
distinctness_correlation: Spearman(AUROC, mean silhouette of held-out type vs rest) and Spearman(AUROC, nearest remaining-type centroid Euclidean) in LOTO PCA on non-test (train+cal) cells
depth_control: library-size residual AUROC of novelty score ⊥ log1p(nCount_RNA) for the 3 best and 3 worst scored types by AUROC
scope: within-atlas leave-one-type-out novelty on a heart atlas; labels are benchmark labels only, not clinical calls
do_not_claim: this sweep reopens or overturns the SC30 STOP

honest_reading: SC33 is a new within-atlas type-novelty estimand on the heart atlas, not a re-opening of the SC30 fetal-cardiomyocyte STOP. Primary adult sweep (held D2, cal D3): 14/15 scored types have novelty AUROC CI-lo > 0.5; median 0.911 range [0.515, 0.951]. protocol does not replicate on this atlas: median AUROC 0.911 is outside 0.777±0.10. Failures: ['unknown']. 1/1 failures lack a close sibling; the SC31 mechanism claim (types inside another type's manifold fail) weakens on this atlas Fetal-only secondary is reported separately and is not the replication verdict. Labels are benchmark labels, not clinical calls. fm_embed=false, cuda=false.
